# v0.23.2-rc3 — lossless default, security, and instrument-integrity release candidate

**RELEASE CANDIDATE — not GA.** This prerelease enters the RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet
(bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md): Phase A (all-tools live matrix on a fresh clone across
privacy postures, planted-secret battery), Phase B (multi-agent P0/P1 sweep of the full
v0.23.1→rc1 diff), Phase C (30+ turn live session soak). GA follows only with all three
receipts green.

## Lossless by default: the privacy split (#346 → #374)

LCM sells lossless memory, and v0.23.2 makes that the shipped default everywhere. Durable
sensitive-pattern redaction (`LCM_SENSITIVE_PATTERNS_ENABLED`) is now a fully independent,
opt-in-forever choice: it is off by default and no other feature turns it on. Cloud embedding
no longer requires it — known cloud providers instead protect only the **provider-bound
copy** of your text, controlled by the new `LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED` flag (unset =
auto-on for cloud). Your durable history stays byte-for-byte lossless while the text leaving
the machine is transformed. Operators who want raw provider payloads can opt out explicitly
with `LCM_EMBEDDING_PRIVACY_ENABLED=false`, which binds vectors to the distinguished
`privacy:off` revision. Changing posture changes vector identity: dispatch refuses until a
new `/lcm embed warmup` registers it, and existing vectors stay ineligible until
`/lcm embed backfill --apply` re-embeds them — LCM never re-embeds automatically.

Rerank payloads are covered by the same resolution (#371): with reranking enabled on a cloud
provider, the rerank query and every snippet are transformed before transport, and ranking
maps back to the original untransformed hits.

## Security: PEM private-key redaction hardening (#365 → #366)

v0.23.1's privacy release contained an ordering flaw: an assignment-style prefix
(`password:` / `passphrase=`) before a PEM block could consume the `-----BEGIN` marker and ship
the private-key body to the cloud embedding provider and durable storage. No customer exposure:
the repository is pre-release with no external deployments; vectors embedded under the previous
transform become ineligible (privacy revision v1 → v3) until the standard
`/lcm embed warmup` + `/lcm embed backfill --apply` sequence re-embeds them.

The fix went through twenty-five adversarial cross-model review rounds and grew into a rewrite of the
redaction scanner around a normalized line model with a **declared threat model** (module
comment): accidental leakage of PEM-structured material in realistic paste/log/transcript shapes
— line-separator and whitespace variants, indentation and label/log prefixes, truncation,
stripped markers, re-wrapped widths, RFC 1421 encrypted-key armor, JSON/log serialization at any
escaping depth, and their compositions — with the dispatch validator as a fail-closed second
layer on the cloud path. Deliberate re-encoding remains out of scope for any content-based
redactor. Performance is linear and bounded (pathological inputs that took 13.9–34.6s now run in
milliseconds; CodeQL ReDoS finding closed).

**rc2 (#383/#384):** the v0.23.2-rc1 Phase-A gauntlet caught a residual the #366 rewrite missed —
a truncated PRIVATE KEY body sharing a line with a following inline PEM marker (any armor label)
escaped to the provider copy, and the residual validator missed it. rc2 closes it at both layers:
the scanner redacts leading base64-body runs before inline markers, and — the durable fix — the
validator became marker-INDEPENDENT (blocking a dispatch where a key-body fragment survives beside a
surviving private-key marker). rc2 also added a placeholder-adjacency backstop; that specific form was
over-broad and was reworked in rc3 (below) — the rc-first gate working as intended, the leak never in a GA build.

**rc3 (#389 + audit + cross-model review):** rc2's gauntlet then caught the fix's own over-reach — a
redacted private key beside a nearby git SHA (ubiquitous in runbooks) refused to embed. rc3 reworks the
placeholder-adjacency backstop to key on a full-width base64 BODY token (>=40 chars, non-English,
excluding pure-hex git-SHA / hash digests) within a bidirectional 160-char window of a private_key
placeholder — serialization-aware, linear bounded-window scan, escape-spelling symmetry regression.
That keeps every orphaned key-body fragment blocked (prefixed log/label lines, bodies glued to or above
the placeholder) while common key+hash prose embeds. A five-auditor audit and an independent cross-model
review verified the full train; their findings — a serialized-escape blind spot and a
prefixed/glued/backward orphan leak class in the first drafts of this fix — were closed before the cut,
and the Phase-A planted-secret battery was extended to cover the full-width body class it could not
exercise before. Single sub-threshold (<40-char) fragments near a placeholder remain the #389 boundary.

## Instrument integrity: loud privacy failures + production-posture harness (#367 → #370)

- `lcm_recall` no longer silently degrades to FTS-only on a privacy-policy configuration error —
  the error is loud at every handler site, and the proactive-recall path surfaces it via a
  dedicated status counter plus a once-per-engine-instance warning.
- The V1-M harness now runs cloud providers at production posture — post-#374 that means the
  lossless-durable / protected-provider-copy split: the transform applies to every cloud-bound
  payload (documents, queries, probes), vector identities register under the active privacy
  revision, resume artifacts bind the posture and refuse mismatches, and non-embedding runs
  keep a byte-identical raw corpus.
- Provider aliases (`openai`, `siliconflow`) can no longer bypass the cloud-privacy predicate.

## Release process: rc-first gauntlet (#373)

Any release containing product code is now rc-first: this prerelease is the first through the
three-phase live gauntlet, and the GA commit may differ from the passing rc tree only by the
added release notes. The Phase-A runner discovers the tool surface at runtime (15 tools),
binds release runs to a clean tree at the exact rc tag, and records hermes provenance in its
receipt.
